svg.text: Graphs needing n pieces: d(G) = n on 7 and 8 vertices
d(G) = fewest simple cycles + single edges partitioning E(G). Exhaustive: 1044 graphs (n = 7), 12346 (n = 8), 274668 (n = 9). Filled dots = the three hubs.
How many graphs have d(G) - (n - 1) = k
k = d(G) - (n - 1); k = +1 means d(G) = n
n = 8: all 4 graphs with d(G) = 8 (none has d(G) > 8)
K3 v I4 + pendant at a hub
K3 v I4 + pendant at a leaf
Coloured solid = one cycle each; grey dashed = single edges. Every odd-degree vertex needs a single edge, which is what the lower bound counts.
n = 9: max d = 9, attained by exactly 16 graphs (e.g. K3 v I6); still no graph reaches n + 1.
